gaps.sentence: He ___ to the reporters that the deal was off.
gaps.explanation: 'Said to the reporters that...' is correct; tell cannot be followed by 'to'.

gaps.sentence: 'I've already spoken to the insurers,' he reminded me. He reminded me that he ___ spoken to the insurers.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect: had already spoken.

gaps.sentence: 'You must be joking!' I exclaimed. I exclaimed that he ___ be joking.
gaps.hint: must of deduction does not backshift
gaps.explanation: Must expressing confident deduction usually stays must; only obligation shifts to had to.

gaps.sentence: "I am sorry I am late." — He ___ for being late.
gaps.explanation: 'Apologise for doing something' reports an apology.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll definitely pay you back,' he said. He ___ to pay me back.
gaps.explanation: Promises take promise + to-infinitive: promised to pay me back.
Apologise for + -ing; the other verbs do not take 'for + -ing' in this pattern.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't touch the thermostat,' the technician warned us. The technician warned us ___ the thermostat.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands are reported with 'warned + object + not to + infinitive'.

gaps.sentence: 'I have to catch the last train,' she said. She said she ___ catch the last train.
gaps.explanation: Have to (obligation) backshifts to had to after a past reporting verb.
